The clusters are laid on each other by the central molecule; a neighbouring molecule matches when the nearest one in the second crystal is shifted by at most 20 % of its distance from the centre and turned by at most 20° (the tolerances of COMPACK, Chisholm, Motherwell, 2005). Then the matched molecules are laid together: the RMSD of their atoms (without H). 15 of 15 and tenths of Å — one packing; fewer — another form.
